title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Number of Originals Lodged Back for a Correction
content:
When the paper originals of a `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` set are lodged back with the line in connection with a correction, the lodgement entry records a number of originals. This page defines that number as a balance drawn from the document's documentation history.

## Definition

The number of originals handed in is the balance of originals the documentation history shows as still circulating on the document. It is worked out over the document's entire history, from its first set onwards, and it is never taken from a figure the caller supplies:

- take the total of originals on every entry that records originals put into circulation on the document;
- deduct the total of originals on every entry that records originals surrendered to the line;
- deduct the total of originals on every entry that records originals declared void;
- if the result would fall below zero, the balance is zero.

The balance is counted in whole originals.

## Why the whole history gives the current set

An earlier set on a document is always completely returned or declared void before a later set is issued. The balance over the entire history is therefore identical to the count of the current set's originals still circulating.

## Worked examples (hypothetical histories)

| Entries in the documentation history | Balance |
|---|---|
| Set 1: 3 originals put into circulation | 3 |
| Set 1: 3 put into circulation; 1 surrendered | 2 |
| Set 1: 3 put into circulation, 3 surrendered; set 2: 3 put into circulation | 3 |
| Set 1: 3 put into circulation, 1 surrendered, 2 declared void; set 2: 3 put into circulation, 2 surrendered | 1 |
| No entry putting originals into circulation | 0 |

In the fourth line, six originals were put into circulation in total; three were surrendered and two declared void, so six less three less two leaves one.

## Points of judgement

**The shipper says it holds two originals, but the history balance is three. Which figure is recorded?** The history balance of three; the caller's own count is not used.

**Entries from an earlier set are in the history. Are they left out?** No. Every entry of the document counts; because each earlier set was fully returned or voided, its entries cancel out.
